name: MHRA seizes £2m of fake weight loss pens
summary: The MHRA and West Midlands Police seized counterfeit weight loss pens worth about £2 million in Birmingham, including fake retatrutide and tirzepatide products.
keyPoints: The MHRA and West Midlands Police seized counterfeit weight loss medicines worth about £2 million in a raid on an industrial unit in Birmingham on 14 October.
The haul included more than 12,000 counterfeit retatrutide and tirzepatide pens.
The MHRA says the products have not been assessed for safety, quality or effectiveness.
The MHRA says retatrutide is not authorised for use in the UK.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: The MHRA says it worked with West Midlands Police to seize counterfeit weight loss medicines worth about £2 million from an industrial unit in Birmingham. Officers took more than 12,000 counterfeit retatrutide and tirzepatide pens, plus packaging for around 30,000 more products.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: The MHRA says the products have not been assessed for safety, quality or effectiveness, and that there is no guarantee of what they contain or whether they are contaminated with harmful substances. It also says retatrutide is not authorised for use in the UK and that products sold as retatrutide outside legitimate clinical trials are being supplied illegally and could pose serious risks to public health.
